title: Expired or forged access tokens are refused with distinct stable-coded reasons
asA: operator whose project receives an access token that fails one of the standard invariants
iWant: the JWT verifier to refuse the token before it can lift into a Principal
soThat: no session is issued and no protected route runs against an unverified identity

acceptanceCriteria.description: A token whose `exp` claim is in the past is refused with `KEYCLOAK_JWT_EXPIRED` and no session is issued.
acceptanceCriteria.given: a JWT verifier warm against the realm's JWKS and an access token whose `exp` claim was minted 60 seconds before the test-injected clock's current time
acceptanceCriteria.then: the response is a 4xx with body error code `KEYCLOAK_JWT_EXPIRED`; no session cookie is set on the response; the audit log records one `keycloak.jwt_refused` event carrying realmSlug and reason class `expired` and no token value

acceptanceCriteria.description: A token signed under a key not published by the realm at any point in the test's window is refused with `KEYCLOAK_JWT_SIGNATURE_INVALID` after exactly one JWKS refresh.
acceptanceCriteria.given: a JWT verifier and a token signed by a key that was never on any JWKS response the realm returned
acceptanceCriteria.then: the verifier observes one JWKS refresh against the injected httpFetch, then refuses the token with `KEYCLOAK_JWT_SIGNATURE_INVALID`; no session cookie is set; the audit log records one `keycloak.jwt_refused` event carrying realmSlug and reason class `signature`; the reason class is `signature`, not `kid-unknown` (the kid appears in JWKS; the signature under that kid does not verify)
